lines.text: A pond goes from ninety percent goldfish down to eighty percent. How many goldfish leave?
lines.caption: A pond goes from ninety percent goldfish down to eighty percent. How many goldfish leave?

lines.text: Most kids guess ten. The real answer is much bigger!

lines.text: Hello, I'm Vantee! Let's go fishing for the answer.

lines.text: Here's the question.
lines.caption: Here's the question.

lines.text: A pond has two hundred fish.
lines.caption: A pond has two hundred fish.

lines.text: Ninety percent of them are goldfish.
lines.caption: Ninety percent of them are goldfish.

lines.text: How many goldfish must be taken out so that eighty percent of the fish left are goldfish?
lines.caption: How many goldfish must be taken out so that eighty percent of the fish left are goldfish?

lines.caption: So what do we know? Two hundred fish, and ninety percent are goldfish.

lines.text: We only take out goldfish. The other fish all stay in the pond.
lines.caption: We only take out goldfish. The other fish all stay in the pond.

lines.text: At the end, eighty percent of the fish that are LEFT must be goldfish.

scenes.chapter: Solution 1: watch the fish that stay

lines.text: Welcome back! Here's the strategy: watch the fish that don't change.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Here's the strategy: watch the fish that don't change.

lines.text: Ten percent of two hundred is twenty. So ninety percent is nine times twenty, one hundred eighty goldfish.
lines.caption: Ten percent of two hundred is twenty. So ninety percent is nine times twenty, one hundred eighty goldfish.

lines.text: That leaves twenty other fish.
lines.caption: That leaves twenty other fish.

lines.text: Here's the key. We never take out those twenty fish. They stay, no matter what.
lines.caption: Here's the key. We never take out those twenty fish. They stay, no matter what.

lines.text: At the end, eighty percent are goldfish. So the other fish make up twenty percent.
lines.caption: At the end, eighty percent are goldfish. So the other fish make up twenty percent.

lines.text: Twenty percent is the same as one out of five.
lines.caption: Twenty percent is the same as one out of five.

lines.text: So our twenty other fish are one fifth of the pond. The whole pond is five times twenty, one hundred fish.
lines.caption: So our twenty other fish are one fifth of the pond. The whole pond is five times twenty, one hundred fish.

lines.text: We started with two hundred fish and end with one hundred. So one hundred goldfish were taken out.
lines.caption: We started with two hundred fish and end with one hundred. So one hundred goldfish were taken out.

lines.text: Check: eighty goldfish out of one hundred fish. That's eighty percent!
lines.caption: Check: eighty goldfish out of one hundred fish. That's eighty percent!

lines.text: Here's another way. Think of a ratio.

lines.text: Eighty percent goldfish and twenty percent others. That's four goldfish for every one other fish.
lines.caption: Eighty percent goldfish and twenty percent others. That's four goldfish for every one other fish.

lines.text: There are twenty other fish, so there must be four times twenty, eighty goldfish.
lines.caption: There are twenty other fish, so there must be four times twenty, eighty goldfish.

lines.text: We had one hundred eighty goldfish, and we need eighty. Take out one hundred. Same answer!
lines.caption: We had one hundred eighty goldfish, and we need eighty. Take out one hundred. Same answer!

lines.text: When would you pick this way? When the percents turn into a neat ratio, like four to one.
lines.caption: When would you pick this way? When the percents turn into a neat ratio, like four to one.

lines.text: Now let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.
lines.caption: Now let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.

lines.text: Choice A, ten, is ninety minus eighty. But that's a difference of percents, not a number of fish!
lines.caption: Choice A, ten, is ninety minus eighty. But that's a difference of percents, not a number of fish!

lines.text: Here's a quick test. The twenty others must be one fifth of the fish left.
lines.caption: Here's a quick test. The twenty others must be one fifth of the fish left.

lines.text: Take out ten, and one hundred ninety are left. One fifth of that is thirty-eight, not twenty.
lines.caption: Take out ten, and one hundred ninety are left. One fifth of that is thirty-eight, not twenty.

lines.text: Choice B, twenty, is the number of other fish, not the number to take out.

lines.text: One hundred eighty left, so one fifth of that is thirty-six.

lines.text: Choice C, forty: one hundred sixty left, so one fifth of that is thirty-two.
lines.caption: Choice C, forty: one hundred sixty left, so one fifth of that is thirty-two.

lines.text: Choice D, fifty: one hundred fifty left, one fifth is thirty.
lines.caption: Choice D, fifty: one hundred fifty left, one fifth is thirty.

lines.text: Only one hundred works: one hundred left, and one fifth is exactly twenty.

lines.text: So here's a great habit. Find the group that doesn't change, and build from it.
lines.caption: So here's a great habit. Find the group that doesn't change, and build from it.

lines.text: When only one kind of thing is removed, the other kind stays the same.
